module_title: The 4 New Labour Codes: Foundational Framework
introduction: This foundational level explores India's historic overhaul of its labor jurisprudence. To balance 'Ease of Doing Business' with universal worker welfare, the Central Government consolidated 29 complex, overlapping, and archaic central labor laws into four streamlined Codes.

core_concepts.title: The Great Consolidation (The 4 Codes)
core_concepts.description:
1. The Code on Wages, 2019 (Consolidates 4 Acts like Minimum Wages Act, Payment of Wages Act).
2. The Industrial Relations (IR) Code, 2020 (Consolidates 3 Acts including the Industrial Disputes Act).
3. The Code on Social Security, 2020 (Consolidates 9 Acts including EPF, ESI, and Maternity Benefit).
4. The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code, 2020 (Consolidates 13 Acts including the Factories Act).

core_concepts.title: The Code on Wages, 2019
core_concepts.description:
Historically, minimum wages were only guaranteed for certain 'scheduled employments'.
- The Paradigm Shift: The Code universalizes the provisions of minimum wages and timely payment of wages to ALL employees, irrespective of the sector or wage ceiling. It ensures every worker in India has a statutory right to a minimum wage.

core_concepts.title: National Floor Wage
core_concepts.description:
A new statutory safety net designed to prevent states from competing in a 'race to the bottom' to attract cheap industry.
- The Rule: The Central Government fixes a minimum 'Floor Wage' based on minimum living standards. State Governments MUST set their state minimum wages equal to or higher than this Floor Wage. If a state's minimum wage is already higher, they cannot lower it to match the floor.

core_concepts.title: Code on Social Security, 2020
core_concepts.description: Expands the reach of social security mechanisms (Provident Fund, Gratuity, Medical Insurance) beyond the organized sector. For the first time, the unorganized sector, self-employed workers, and home-based workers are legally integrated into the social security framework through targeted welfare funds.

important_entities.name: Universal Application
important_entities.significance: Under the old Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the government had to constantly update a 'schedule' of specific industries that were subject to minimum wage laws. The new Wage Code abolishes this, making minimum wage a universal right for every worker across India.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The 'Floor Wage vs Minimum Wage' Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will ask: 'Can a State Government set its minimum wage at ₹400 if the Central Floor Wage is ₹500?' **NO**. The Floor Wage is the absolute statutory baseline. States can set their minimum wage higher (e.g., ₹600), but never lower than the National Floor Wage.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: W I S O (Wages, IR, Social Security, OSH)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember WISO to quickly list the four pillars of the modern Indian labor framework.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a Judiciary question asks 'Which Code guarantees minimum wages to all workers irrespective of the sector?', select the **Code on Wages, 2019**.
